title: The 1-Page Marketing Plan: Get New Customers, Make More Money, And Stand out From The Crowd
author: Allan Dib
target_audience: Anyone interested in practical marketing strategies
primary_purpose: To provide a straightforward, actionable framework for small and medium-sized businesses to create and implement an effective marketing plan using a single-page template.

structure_format.narrative_style: Clear, practical, and direct with a conversational tone
structure_format.organization: Structured around the nine squares of the 1-Page Marketing Plan canvas, grouped into three main phases: Before, During, and After

key_concepts_lessons: Marketing planning doesn’t have to be complex—clarity and action matter most.
Dividing prospects and customers into stages (Attract, Convert, and Delight) clarifies what actions to take.
Identifying and targeting an ideal customer is essential for success.
Effective messaging that resonates with the target market makes a marketing plan work.
Using lead capture and nurturing systems increases conversion rates.
Consistent follow-up, nurturing, and delivering value create loyal customers and repeat business.
notable_features: 1-Page Marketing Plan canvas as a central tool
Realistic advice for small business realities
cultural_historical_context: Published in the mid-2010s during an era where digital marketing complexity was rising, the book provided a much-needed simplified, results-focused roadmap for non-marketers and small businesses.
reception_impact: Became a bestseller in marketing and small business categories
Widely praised for its simplicity and clarity
Adopted by thousands of entrepreneurs as a template for marketing success
Some critics note it is less suitable for large enterprises or highly advanced marketers
comparable_titles: Building a StoryBrand by Donald Miller
Made to Stick by Chip Heath & Dan Heath
Duct Tape Marketing by John Jantsch
